text:
Ivy: morning — saw a noisy-neighbor spike in ap-south-1 around 03:12 UTC. tenant 'orbit' started concurrent prefill jobs and NIC egress on rack-7 hit 94%. p95 up ~2.5x.
Marco: ouch. any slab evictions?
Ivy: small HBM_evictions bump and kvcache_miss_rate doubled. NVLINK jitter occasional.
Chen: quick fix = throttle prefill qps per-tenant, but that delays critical jobs. Long-term: propose a 'rotor' containment — short-lived ephemeral slices staggered across racks to spread egress/thermal load.
Lina: rotor sounds like pinwheel/carousel cousin. how is it different?
Chen: rotor emphasizes short hops with warmup window and prefers racks with spare NIC headroom and low recent thermal excursions. hops = 3 mins by default.
Marco: scheduler impact? need tenant tag + allocation annotation. Also runtime flags for rotor.enabled and rotor.hop_minutes.
Ivy: metrics to watch: per-rack egress_pct, hbm_evictions, kvcache_miss_rate, p95_tokens. Alert when any > 80% for > 1m.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: infra/rotor-controller -> canary tenant 'rotor-canary' in ap-south-1 at 05:00 UTC.
Lina: owners? Chen will do controller, Marco handles scheduler integration, Ivy observes canary and incident comms. I'll draft a short cost estimate for token churn.
Ivy: agree. start with instrumentation + alerting. If rotor triggers > 3x/day for a tenant, auto-generate SRE ticket recommending dedicated carveout.
Marco: ok. PRs incoming. Tagging @Chen @Lina @Ivy.
